clue.text: Ultimately you will get commended and promoted

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word you, its end

parts.note: commended means praised

explanation.surface: A promise that in the end your good work will be praised and you will get a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something promoted has been raised up, lifted in rank or position, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Game show

definitions.meaning: a solitary card game, called solitaire in North America
Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera of that name is a stage show

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase, 'Game show' suggests television quizzes; split it into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the card game played alone and the title of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, a staged show.

clue.text: Excessive light may need adjustment

indicators.note: something needing adjustment must be rearranged, so the letters of the two words are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lamp that is too bright may need its setting changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Almighty is informal for very great or extreme, as in an almighty row, so it matches excessive.

clue.text: Band of regiment (horse)

parts.note: the SAS, Special Air Service, is a British army regiment
horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H

explanation.surface: A ribbon worn by members of a cavalry regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'horse' looks like a gloss on a cavalry regiment, but it is slang for heroin, giving H.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist, so band is a synonym.

clue.text: Rodents want somewhere to sleep and something to eat

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a room for sleeping
an ice is an ice cream or sorbet, something eaten

explanation.surface: Small animals need a bed and some food.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse is a small hibernating rodent, so the plural form names rodents.

clue.text: Dilapidated farm was not one of little substance

indicators.note: dilapidated means falling apart, so the letters of the words are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rundown farm was not much of a property.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a weak figure without real substance, as a straw effigy has nothing inside it.

clue.text: Suitable furnishings applied to middle of home

indicators.note: applied to puts the furnishings word in front of the next piece, attached to it

parts.note: decor is the furnishings and decoration of a room

indicators.note: middle of says to drop the outer letters of a synonym for home

parts.note: a house is a home

explanation.surface: Fitting furniture and fabrics have been placed in the central rooms of a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' acts on HOUSE, a synonym, not a printed word: taking off its first and last letters leaves OUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorous means proper and in keeping with good taste, which is a sense of suitable.

clue.text: Place for training an official before a series of competitions

indicators.note: before places the official ahead of the final single letter

parts.note: a gym is where people train
a khan is a ruler or official in Central Asia

explanation.surface: A venue where an official prepares ahead of a run of contests.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'an' in 'an official' is only a link; the final A comes from 'a' after 'before'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymkhana is an event made up of a series of competitions, typically horse riding contests for children.

clue.text: Old man in charge of park — unknown fruit is grown here

parts.note: a park ranger looks after a park
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: An elderly park keeper raises some mysterious fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' looks like a single unit (PA, OM); split it so 'man' joins 'in charge of park'.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glass building where orange trees and other fruit are grown.

clue.text: A skinflint about to produce spray

indicators.note: about means going round, so a miser and the article surround the little word to

parts.note: a skinflint is a miser, someone mean with money

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted person is about to make a spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of'; instead A MISER goes about TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device that turns a liquid into a fine spray, as in a perfume bottle.

clue.text: Grouse, exhibiting low resistance to nonsense

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
cock is slang for nonsense, as in poppycock

explanation.surface: Someone complaining, showing little patience with rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like a verb for complaining; it is the game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A moorcock is a male red grouse, found on moorland.

clue.text: Drinks may be ruined

definitions.meaning: drinks may be served over ice cubes
a marriage or business that has failed is said to be wrecked like a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means served over ice and, idiomatically, in ruin, as a ship broken on a reef.

clue.text: Demotion -— large one ——- it is staggering

indicators.note: something staggering lurches about, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge downgrade, an astonishing one.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegation is moving down to a lower rank or division, a synonym of demotion, used of football teams in Britain.

clue.text: Corruption put before a court

indicators.note: put before places the decay word in front of the single letter

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: Bribery is laid before a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a court' seems to go together; the definition is just 'court'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rota is the Roman Catholic Church's supreme court of appeal, so it names a court.

clue.text: In relation to transport, behave greenly

parts.note: re means concerning, in relation to
a cycle is a bicycle, a means of transport

explanation.surface: Advice to act in an environmentally friendly way when travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Recycling is the classic environmentally friendly act, so to recycle is to behave greenly.

clue.text: Engineers face palliative

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
the dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Engineers confront a remedy that eases pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineers' is usually RE in crosswords; here the longer corps abbreviation REME is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial means giving relief or acting as a remedy, close to palliative in sense.

clue.text: Hangs out with crooks and scraps

parts.note: cons are convicts, crooks
orts are scraps of food left over

explanation.surface: Someone spends time with criminals and fights.
explanation.definitionFit: To consort with someone is to keep company with them, which is to hang out with them.

clue.text: Flower given away with note is returned

parts.note: something given away is free

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the note and the word is are read backwards

parts.note: A is a musical note

explanation.surface: A complimentary flower comes with a note that is sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the A and IS together, giving SIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The freesia is a fragrant flowering plant of the iris family.

clue.text: Foreigner able to exchange a rupee? No

indicators.note: exchange means swapping places, so the letters of the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether a traveller from Europe can change Indian money, and answers no.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits: a European uses euros, so the rupee question is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: From a British or Indian viewpoint, someone from continental Europe is a foreigner.

clue.text: Basic home man has to lease

parts.note: in means at home
he is the pronoun for a man
to lease is to rent

explanation.surface: A simple house where a man must let property.
explanation.definitionFit: Inherent means intrinsic, existing as a basic part of something.

clue.text: Ship used to dock

definitions.meaning: a fast sailing ship of the nineteenth century
shears for cutting hair, to dock being to cut short

explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' suggests mooring a ship; here it means cutting short.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fast sailing ship and a cutting tool used to trim or dock tails and hair.

clue.text: Large sum of money producing a fraction of the optimum interest

indicators.note: fraction of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A big sum earns only a small part of the best possible return.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'producing', which is a link word between definition and wordplay; the definition is 'Large sum of money'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint is informal for a vast amount of money, as in making a mint.

clue.text: Novelist using girl's name

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl, here with the possessive
a name, like a worthy, is a notable person

explanation.surface: A writer borrows a woman's name.
explanation.walkthrough: John Galsworthy wrote The Forsyte Saga.
explanation.definitionFit: John Galsworthy was an English novelist and Nobel laureate, author of The Forsyte Saga.

clue.text: Coming back, favourites cross the threshold

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the whole pair of pieces reads backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites
a rood is a cross, as in a church's rood screen

explanation.surface: Returning, the favourite people step over the threshold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming back' turns PETSROOD as a whole into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep is the step at the entrance of a house, its threshold.

clue.text: Worthless group of people, 100 in all

indicators.note: in places the Roman hundred inside the total

parts.note: sum means the whole, all
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Describes a bad crowd of a hundred people in total.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a contemptuous term for people regarded as worthless.

clue.text: One who chooses the Spanish or American fish

parts.note: a picker is one who picks or chooses
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone selecting between Spanish and American fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link here, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pickerel is a small pike of North American waters, so it is an American fish.

clue.text: Creature has to run away — it runs very quickly

parts.note: an ant is a creature
to elope is to run away to marry

explanation.surface: A creature must flee because it is so fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are fleet-footed animals famous for their speed in running.

clue.text: Contemplate miniature, one dropped and shattered

indicators.note: something shattered is broken to pieces, so the remaining letters are rearranged
dropped means let fall, so one letter is removed

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A small painting falls and is smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one dropped' removes an I from MINIATURE, leaving MNIATURE, which 'shattered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to think deeply, so it means to contemplate.
